subject: Discovery recap & next steps — NovaMed proprietary API migration
summary: Post-call discovery recap from Laura confirming NovaMed's current OpenAI usage, key pain points (latency, cost, auditability), success criteria, and proposed shortlist of open models plus next steps for a technical POC and procurement timeline.
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Maya Patel <maya@novamed.com>, Ethan Collins <ethan.collins@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — NovaMed proprietary API migration

Hi Maya / Ethan —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking us through NovaMed's current setup and constraints. Below is a concise recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Meeting highlights (from our call):
- Current stack: NovaMed primarily routes clinical summarization requests through OpenAI (gpt-4o) via a proprietary API gateway; Anthropic used for a small subset of creative/marketing content.
- Volume & SLA: ~1.2M tokens/month; 99th percentile latency target for user-facing summaries is 250ms; batch jobs (nightly QA) can tolerate higher latency.
- Primary pain points: rising per-token cost with OpenAI, lack of KV-cache control, limited observability for token-level billing, and audit log requirements for compliance (HIPAA-adjacent).
- Compatibility needs: API parity for instruction-following endpoints, streaming response support, function-calling for structured outputs, and an embeddings pipeline that matches existing vector search fidelity.
- Success criteria for migration: <=10% regression in generation quality (measured on your eval set), matched or improved 99th pctl latency for interactive flows, and predictable 30–60% lower per-token operating cost at steady state.

Model shortlist we discussed (open models to evaluate for POC):
1) Mistral-Open-3 (quantized variant) — strong instruction-following and cost-friendly on A100/RT cores.
2) Llama-3-Chat-16k (8-bit profile) — good streaming and wide community support; requires KV cache tuning.
3) RedWrap-2 (Redwood-curated tuned checkpoint) — candidate for lower-latency specialized summarization (requires evaluation).

Attachments: I attached a one-page compatibility brief and a migration worksheet to capture evaluation metrics and procurement timing. Please fill the worksheet fields marked 'Team input' where helpful.

Proposed next steps (suggested owners & timing):
- Technical POC kickoff (Redwood + NovaMed infra): reproduce 2 representative summary flows on a small dataset — target start: week of Oct 12. Owner: Aditya (Redwood) + Ethan (NovaMed).
- Eval plan: we will run the NovaMed eval set (10K examples) across the three shortlisted models and report quality/lossless metrics + latency/cost. Owner: Ben. Deliverable due Oct 23.
- Security checklist & SOC2 evidence exchange: we will share our audit artifact links; NovaMed to confirm additional evidence required for HIPAA-adjacent review. Owner: Laura.
- Commercial: preliminary sizing & an indicative pricing model for Dedicated vs Hosted — to be shared after POC. Owner: Laura / Sales Ops.

Questions for you before we kick off:
1) Can Ethan share a redacted sample of 200 summaries and the current eval rubric (accuracy/ROUGE/QA pass rate)?
2) Any procurement constraints/process timing (e.g., PO cycles) we should factor into the Oct–Nov window?

If that all looks right, I’ll create a short action tracker and calendar invite for the POC sync.

Thanks —

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: novamed-migration-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-compatibility-brief.pdf (PDF)

Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — NovaMed proprietary API migration

Laura —

Thanks for this write-up; very helpful and accurate summary of the call. A few clarifications:
- Volume: the 1.2M tokens/month is our production user-facing flow only; internal QA and background enrichment add another ~300K tokens/month but can be batched.
- Latency target: 250ms is ideal; we accept up to 400ms during peak.
- Eval rubric: we can share the rubric and a 250-example redacted sample by EOD Wednesday. I’ll ask Ethan to pull the samples.

On procurement: we operate on a quarterly PO cycle — earliest committed spend for a new vendor would be the start of Q1’27 unless we escalate. That said, we are open to a 6–8 week POC that does not require an immediate PO; budget sign-off would follow POC success.

Confirmed: please go ahead with the POC kickoff invite and Ben’s eval plan. We’ll fill the worksheet and return it by Oct 11.

—Maya
